name: com.appstoretracker/mcp
title: App Store Tracker
description: iOS App Store chart rankings, app details, reviews, keywords and revenue estimates.

tools.name: search_apps
tools.description: Find iOS apps by name or keyword, using Apple's iTunes Search API at call time (a text search over Apple's catalogue, not our own data). Returns app_store_id, name, developer, category id, rating, rating count and price for each match. Call this first to turn an app name into the app_store_id (the 'app_id' argument) that every per-app tool needs.

tools.name: get_app_details
tools.description: Get the listing for one iOS app by app_id: name, developer, subtitle, description, version, price, languages, content rating, screenshot URLs, an AI-written short summary, plus the storefront's rating and rating count, its latest recorded chart position (and the one before it), and the latest revenue and downloads estimate. Use this for a single app's current snapshot; use get_ranking_history for positions over time, get_revenue_history for estimates over time and get_timeline for listing changes. Errors with 'App not found' when the id is not in our data. Get the id from search_apps. For several apps (a chart, a competitor list) pass app_ids instead of calling once per app.

app_id.description: App Store ID (numeric ID from the app URL)

app_ids.description: Up to 25 App Store IDs in one call instead of app_id, e.g. every app of a get_rankings chart. Answers { items: [{ app_id, data } or { app_id, error }] }. Each app counts as one call against the monthly limit.

tools.name: get_rankings
tools.description: Get the App Store top free chart for a country, in chart order with #1 first: the overall chart by default, or one category via category_id (see get_categories). Each app comes with its position, previous position, name, developer, rating and revenue and download estimates, and the response gives the chart day it describes. Only top free is collected; top paid and top grossing are not. Use get_ranking_history for how one app's position moved over time.

category_id.description: App Store category ID (default: "36", the overall chart; e.g. "6015" for Finance, "6014" for Games). get_categories lists them.

chart.description: Which chart. Only top_free is collected (top paid and top grossing are not, and return no items), so this is the default and the only option.

tools.name: add_to_watchlist
tools.description: Add an app to your watchlist, and with a keyword_id also track that keyword for the app. A keyword is tracked only for an app on your watchlist. Needs an API key bound to an account.

app_id.description: App Store ID of the app to watch

keyword_id.description: Keyword uuid to track for the app (optional; from the keyword tools)

country_code.description: Two-letter storefront code (default: "us"); with keyword_id it must match the keyword's storefront

tools.name: get_similar_apps
tools.description: Find apps similar in meaning to one app, using embedding similarity over their listings (limited to the given storefront). Each result has rating, rating count, revenue and downloads estimates and a distance (lower means closer). Results are sorted by downloads estimate, biggest first, not by distance. Use it to build a competitor list; use search_apps to look up an app by name instead.

app_id.description: App Store ID of the reference app

limit.description: Maximum number of similar apps (1-50, default: 12)

tools.name: get_reviews
tools.description: Get the newest user reviews of one iOS app in one storefront, newest first: title, text, star rating (rating), author, app version reviewed and date. Read live from Apple's public reviews feed. Use it to read what users say; use get_app_details for the overall rating and rating count. Returns an empty list when there are no reviews, with unavailable: true when Apple's feed could not be read.

app_id.description: App Store ID of the app

tools.name: get_timeline
tools.description: Get every recorded change to one iOS app listing: version, name, subtitle, price, screenshots and description, newest first, with the day each change was first seen.

app_id.description: App Store ID (numeric ID from the app URL)

tools.name: get_categories
tools.description: List every App Store category as a category_id and category_name pair (a fixed list, no arguments, no network call). Use it to find the category_id to pass to get_rankings; the overall chart is category_id 36.

tools.name: get_ranking_history
tools.description: Get one app's top-free chart position per day in one storefront, as ranking_position and created_at points. The chart is the overall chart (category_id 36) when the app holds as many days there as in its own category over the asked span, otherwise its category chart, so a different span can answer from a different chart; category_id in the answer names it. Look back 1 to 3650 days (default 30). Use it for trends and for explaining a move; use get_rankings for a whole chart on one day. Top paid and top grossing history is not collected.

app_id.description: App Store ID of the app

days.description: Number of days of history (1-3650, default: 30)

tools.name: get_revenue_history
tools.description: Get the worldwide monthly downloads and revenue estimates for one iOS app, one point per data month (dated its first day). Values are Sensor Tower buckets; downloadsFloor/revenueFloor mark the stored 1,000, which means "< 5K", not an exact figure. missing_months lists the months between the first and the last point for which we hold no estimate: a gap in our data, not a zero. estimate_break: true marks a month whose revenue is 10x or more, or a tenth or less, of the month before, usually a change in how the estimate is made rather than a real jump (estimate_breaks counts them); compare months on the same side of a break only. For several apps pass app_ids instead of calling once per app.

app_id.description: App Store ID (numeric ID from the app URL)

app_ids.description: Up to 25 App Store IDs in one call instead of app_id, e.g. every app of a get_rankings chart. Answers { items: [{ app_id, data } or { app_id, error }] }. Each app counts as one call against the monthly limit.

range.description: How many data months to return, newest last: 30d = the newest month, 90d = the newest 3, 1y = the newest 12, all = everything

tools.name: get_keywords
tools.description: Get the App Store search terms one iOS app is collected as ranking for in one storefront, with its position, the day that position was observed, and popularity: Apple's own search popularity for the term in that storefront, 1-100, or null when unknown.

app_id.description: App Store ID (numeric ID from the app URL)

tools.name: get_ads
tools.description: Get the ad creatives one iOS app is running, with the ad library each came from and how many that library holds for the app. An ad's landingDomain (the host of its linkUrl) can be passed as host to get_web_funnels to see the recorded web funnel that ad sends people to.

app_id.description: App Store ID (numeric ID from the app URL)

limit.description: About how many ads a page holds (1-100, default: 30). Copies of one creative merge into one ad, so a page can hold more or fewer.

offset.description: Where the page starts, counted in stored ad entries rather than ads (default: 0). For the next page, pass meta.nextOffset.

tools.name: get_tracked_apps
tools.description: Get the apps this API key's own account is monitoring, newest first. Scoped to the caller: a key bound to another account sees a different set, and a key bound to no account is refused.

limit.description: Maximum number of tracked apps (1-1000, default: 200)

tools.name: get_keyword_watchlist
tools.description: Get the keywords this API key's own account has asked us to track, with each keyword's next scheduled SERP sweep. Scoped to the caller, same as get_tracked_apps.

app_id.description: Only return keywords watched for this App Store ID (default: every app the account watches)

tools.name: search_designs
tools.description: Search real iPhone app screens that App Store Tracker captured itself (the library at /designs) by describing what you want to see, e.g. "paywall with a free trial toggle and the yearly plan preselected", "onboarding that asks for the user's goals", "notification permission pre-prompt". Describe one screen in plain words; narrow with pattern or app_id rather than with negations or keyword lists. Ranked by meaning, with exact on-screen words counting extra, and at most per_app screens per app; in deep mode (the default) a model then reads the top 40 and puts the screens that really show what was asked first, each with match true, the rest after with match false. Each item gives the app_id for every per-app tool, the flow and screen it belongs to, a short summary, the image URL and the App Store Tracker page to cite, plus captured_at and app_version of the app's newest capture (null when not recorded) and, on paywall screens we have read, paywall: the plans, prices, trial and buttons on that screen. Covers only the apps we captured, not the whole App Store; an empty list means none of those matched.

query.description: What the screen shows, in plain language (at most 300 characters)

pattern.description: Only screens of this category: onboarding, paywall (paywall & subscription), features (the app itself after first run) or other (settings, account, help...). Default: any

app_id.description: Only this app's screens (App Store ID, from search_apps)

per_app.description: Most screens from one app (1-5, default: 2; ignored with app_id)

offset.description: Screens to skip, for the next page (use next_offset; at most 500, enough for every screen of one app)

mode.description: deep (default): a model checks the top results against the query and moves the real matches first; standard: search order only, a little faster

tools.name: list_design_apps
tools.description: List every app whose screens App Store Tracker captured itself (the library at /designs), best US chart position first, with its screen count, the design categories captured (onboarding, paywall, features, other) and its page. Page through the whole library with offset, or narrow it: by category name, by words in the app's name, by a design category, or by app_ids, which keeps the apps of another answer (for example a get_rankings chart) that we have screens for, in that order. Then search_designs with an app_id shows that app's screens.

category.description: App Store category name, e.g. "Health & Fitness", "Finance", "Games"; ignored when query names an app

query.description: Words in the app's or developer's name (at most 200 characters)

app_ids.description: App Store ids from another answer, best first: only these apps, kept in this order

pattern.description: Only apps with screens of this category

offset.description: Apps to skip, for the next page (use next_offset)

tools.name: get_app_flow
tools.description: Get one app's captured flows (onboarding, paywall, features...) in the order a user meets them, every screen numbered by step with its name, summary, on-screen text, main button and image, so a flow can be rebuilt screen by screen; paywall screens we have read also give paywall: their plans, prices, trial days, preselected plan, close and main button. captured_at, app_version and run_id say which capture the screens come from (null when not recorded); get_design_history has the older captures. The first page also gives walkthroughs: the app's full session recordings, one MP4 per part (guest, signed-in, sign-up...). Each flow gives its animation clips and, on some older captures only, a recording of that flow alone. Every animation clip and flow recording is an MP4 with still frames (frames: time in seconds and image URL) so the motion can be seen without playing the video; frames is empty for a clip not cut into stills yet. Flows come in recording order and keep their flow_no whatever the filter; use pattern for one kind (onboarding is usually what to copy first) or flow_no for one flow. Get the app_id from list_design_apps or search_designs. Needs an active Social Growth Engineers subscription; other keys are refused.

app_id.description: App Store ID of an app we captured (from list_design_apps or search_designs)

pattern.description: Only flows of this category. Default: all

flow_no.description: Only this flow (its flow_no from a previous answer)

frames.description: Include the still frames of each clip (default: true)

offset.description: Flows to skip, for the next page (use next_offset)

tools.name: get_design_history
tools.description: Get the dated captures of one app's paywall and onboarding, newest first, and what changed between them. Each capture (run) gives when it was recorded, the app version on the phone when known (version_source phone, or store for the live store version at capture), archived (true once a newer capture replaced it; its screen files are kept copies), and its flows with every screen's position, file, on-screen text, main button and, on paywall screens we have read, paywall: plans, prices, trial days, preselected plan, close and main button. changes lists what differed between two captures (price, trial, plans, default_plan, close_button, main_button, social_proof, steps, paywall_position, screen_text) with before and after, and a note. A change was observed between two captures of one phone: it can be a redesign, a price change or one arm of an A/B test, and is never proof of a test. An app with no dated capture answers an empty list. Needs an active Social Growth Engineers subscription; other keys are refused.

app_id.description: App Store ID of an app we captured (from list_design_apps or search_designs)

pattern.description: Only paywall or only onboarding flows and changes. Default: both

limit.description: Captures to return, newest first (1-20, default: 5)

tools.name: get_removed_apps
tools.description: List iOS apps that once charted and have disappeared from the App Store, biggest revenue first, updated daily. Each item has the name, developer, category, best chart rank and the store it reached it in, the worldwide monthly revenue and downloads estimates from before the removal (5000 or less means under 5K), first release and last update dates, removed_on (the day we found it gone, not the day Apple acted), restored_on when it came back, and developer_gone when Apple lists no live apps from that developer. The answer also gives totals for the whole list. Needs an active Social Growth Engineers subscription; other keys are refused.

status.description: gone: still missing. back: returned to the store

query.description: Words in the app's or developer's name (at most 200 characters)

category.description: App Store category name, e.g. "Games", "Finance". An unknown name is refused and the error lists the valid ones

country.description: Two-letter code of the store where the app reached its best rank

developer_gone.description: Only apps whose developer has no live apps left

dir.description: Sort direction. Default: biggest, best rank, most recent or A to Z, to suit the sort

offset.description: Apps to skip, for the next page (use next_offset)

tools.name: get_web_funnels
tools.description: Get the web-to-app funnels App Store Tracker recorded in a mobile browser for one app or one landing domain, newest first: every screen from the ad's landing page through quiz questions, email gate and paywall or checkout, with each screen's title, text, answer options, the action taken, its screenshot (image_url) and the prices shown. In pricing, period is the plan's billing unit as recorded and raw is the text on the screen: check a price against raw ("4-Week Plan $19.99" bills every 4 weeks, not weekly). Long funnels run to 70+ screens, so one funnel comes per call by default; next_offset reads the next older one. Pass app_id, or host: a domain or a URL, such as an ad's landingDomain or linkUrl from get_ads; a domain also finds funnels on its subdomains (bitepal.app finds quiz.bitepal.app). An empty list means no funnel was recorded for it.

app_id.description: App Store ID of the app (from search_apps)

host.description: Landing domain or URL, e.g. "bitepal.app" or an ad's linkUrl (at most 200 characters); the path is ignored and subdomains match

limit.description: Funnels to return, newest first (1-3, default: 1); fewer come back when they would make the answer too long

offset.description: Funnels to skip, for the next page (use next_offset)

tools.name: search_web_funnels
tools.description: Search the web-to-app funnels App Store Tracker recorded by words on their screens and prices (every word must appear as written, so "week trial" finds "1-week trial" while "weekly trial" does not; "$6.99", "lose weight"), by funnel builder (funnelfox, appbox, heyflow, custom), by how the funnel ended (paywall, checkout, email gate, App Store redirect), by a screen category or by a screen type (step_type email finds funnels that ask for an email). When no funnel has every word, funnels with any of the words come back instead, those matching the most words first, and the answer says matched: "any_word" (otherwise "all_words"): check matched_steps before treating them as exact. Each app (or host, for a web-only funnel) appears once, as its best recording; other_recordings counts the repeats left out. Complete funnels (ended on a paywall, checkout, email gate or App Store redirect, more than 2 steps) and those with prices come first, newest breaks ties. Each item gives the funnel's app and host, builder, end, prices (period is the billing unit as recorded, raw the screen text to check it against), step count and up to 3 matching screens; get_web_funnels with its host or app_id shows every screen. sort revenue ranks them by the app's revenue estimate instead (we hold no funnel conversion rates). Covers only the funnels we recorded.

query.description: Words to find on the funnel's screens, prices, builder or host, in any order; all must appear, or any when no funnel has all (at most 200 characters)

builder.description: Funnel builder, e.g. funnelfox, appbox, heyflow, custom

pattern.description: Only funnels with a screen of this category: onboarding (quiz, questions, email) or paywall (paywall, checkout, upsell)

step_type.description: Only funnels with a screen of this type, e.g. email (asks for an email), question_multi, upsell

sort.description: match (default): best match first. revenue: the app's newest worldwide monthly revenue estimate first, shown as revenue_estimate (USD); a stand-in for which funnels pay, since we hold no funnel conversion data

offset.description: Funnels to skip, for the next page (use next_offset; at most 500)

tools.name: send_feedback
tools.description: Tell the App Store Tracker team what the user needed and could not get. Call it, without asking first, when no tool can answer the user's question, when a result is wrong, empty or missing data the user expected, or when the user says they wish the server did something; also call it when the user asks to send feedback. Write `request` as one or two plain sentences about what the user was trying to do, not about the tool call. Never include personal data, API keys or private business figures the user shared. Works even when the monthly call limit is reached.

request.description: What the user wanted, in plain words (e.g. "Download estimates for Android apps, not just iOS")

kind.description: missing_capability: no tool covers it; wrong_result: a tool answered wrongly or with gaps; feature_request: the user asked for something new; other

tool.description: The tool involved, when there is one (e.g. "get_revenue_history")

details.description: Optional: what came back and why it fell short (app ids, country, the query used)
